sentences.nl: We gaan weer Nederlandse zinnen oefenen.
Dit zijn de studenten van Marieke.

sentences.en: They live in Rotterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• They live in Rotterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ze" is a pronoun meaning "they."  
• "Wonen" is the verb "to live" in the present tense, third-person plural.  
• "In" is a preposition meaning "in."  
• Dutch often uses the same word order as English in simple sentences: subject + verb + location.  

Examples:  
• Ze werken in Amsterdam. (They work in Amsterdam.)  
• Hij woont in een groot huis. (He lives in a big house.)  
• Wij studeren aan de universiteit. (We study at the university.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ze eten vaak in dat restaurant. (They often eat in that restaurant.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Rotterdam is known for its modern architecture and is a major port city in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: De studenten komen met de trein.
sentences.en: The students come by train.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students come with the train.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De studenten" is the subject and is plural, meaning "the students."  
• "Komen" is the plural form of the verb "komen" (to come) in the present tense.  
• "Met de trein" means "with the train," where "met" is a preposition meaning "with," "de" is the definite article "the," and "trein" means "train."

• Example 1: "Wij gaan met de bus." (We go by bus.)  
• Example 2: "Hij komt met een taxi." (He comes by taxi.)  
• Example 3: "Zij reist met het vliegtuig." (She travels by plane.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De leraar arriveert met de auto." (The teacher arrives by car.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
Dutch public transportation, like trains, is a common and efficient way for students to travel, especially in urban areas. The train network in the Netherlands is extensive and well-connected, making it a popular choice for daily commutes.

sentences.en: Martin cycles to the station.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Martin bikes to the station.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Fietst" is the third person singular present tense of "fietsen," meaning "to bike" or "to cycle."  
• "Naar" is a preposition meaning "to." It's used to indicate direction or destination.  
• Word order in Dutch is subject-verb-object, similar to English for main clauses. 

• Additional Examples:  
  - "Zij loopt naar school." (She walks to school.)  
  - "Wij rijden naar het strand." (We drive to the beach.)  
  - "Ik ga naar de winkel." (I go to the store.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Lisa loopt naar het park." (Lisa walks to the park.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Cycling is a very common mode of transport in the Netherlands due to the flat terrain and extensive cycling infrastructure. It's typical for people to bike to work, school, or other destinations.

sentences.nl: Hij zet zijn fiets in de fietsenstalling.
sentences.en: He puts his bicycle in the bike shed.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He puts his bicycle in the bicycle parking.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij zet" uses the verb "zetten" (to put), which is a regular verb.  
• "zijn fiets" means "his bicycle," showing possession.  
• "in de fietsenstalling" translates to "in the bicycle parking," where "in" is a preposition indicating location.  

Additional Examples:  
• "Zij zet haar boek op de tafel." (She puts her book on the table.)  
• "Wij zetten de planten in de tuin." (We put the plants in the garden.)  
• "De jongen zet zijn tas naast de deur." (The boy puts his bag next to the door.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Zij zet haar tas in de kast." (She puts her bag in the closet.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, it's common to have designated bicycle parking areas or "fietsenstallingen," as cycling is a primary mode of transportation.

sentences.nl: In de fietsenstalling staan heel veel fietsen.
sentences.en: There are a lot of bicycles in the bike parking.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In the bicycle storage stand very many bicycles.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "In de fietsenstalling" is a prepositional phrase indicating location. "Fietsenstalling" is a compound noun combining "fiets" (bicycle) and "stalling" (storage).  
• "Staan" is the plural form of the verb "staan" (to stand), used here to describe the position of multiple objects.  
• "Heel veel" means "very many" or "a lot of," emphasizing the quantity.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Op de tafel liggen heel veel boeken." (On the table lie very many books.)  
  - "In de koelkast staan heel veel flessen." (In the fridge stand very many bottles.)  
  - "Op het plein staan heel veel mensen." (In the square stand very many people.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Op het strand liggen heel veel schelpen." (On the beach lie very many shells.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Bicycle storage facilities, known as "fietsenstalling," are common in the Netherlands, especially in urban areas and near train stations, reflecting the country's strong cycling culture.

sentences.nl: In Amsterdam heeft iedereen een fiets.
sentences.en: In Amsterdam, everyone has a bicycle.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In Amsterdam has everyone a bike.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present perfect tense ("heeft") but in this context, it's used in a present simple sense because "heeft" here means "has" rather than "has had."  
• Word order is subject-verb-object (SVO), but the sentence starts with an adverbial phrase ("In Amsterdam"), causing inversion where the verb comes before the subject.  
• "Iedereen" is an indefinite pronoun meaning "everyone."  
• Examples:  
  - In Nederland regent het vaak. (In the Netherlands, it rains often.)  
  - In de zomer gaan we naar het strand. (In the summer, we go to the beach.)  
  - In de winter is het koud. (In the winter, it is cold.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• In Rotterdam woont mijn tante. (In Rotterdam, my aunt lives.)

## 4. Culture Note  
• Bicycles are a primary mode of transportation in the Netherlands, especially in cities like Amsterdam. Owning a bike is very common due to the country's flat terrain and excellent cycling infrastructure.

sentences.en: Martin walks to the platform.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Martin walks to the platform.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Loopt" is the third person singular present tense form of "lopen," meaning "to walk".  
• The preposition "naar" means "to" or "towards," indicating direction.  
• "Het perron" means "the platform," with "het" being the definite article for neuter nouns.

• Example sentences:  
  - "Zij loopt naar de winkel." (She walks to the store.)  
  - "Ik loop naar huis." (I walk home.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Johan rent naar het station." (Johan runs to the station.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, public transportation is very common, and platforms ("perrons") at train stations are frequently used by commuters.

sentences.nl: Daar is de trein uit Rotterdam.
Waar zijn de studenten? — Ah! Daar zijn de studenten.
Vandaag laat ik de stad zien.

sentences.en: Do you guys like that? — Yes!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Find you that fun? — Yes!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vinden" is the verb "to find," which is used here in a sense of opinion or perception.  
• "Jullie" is the subject pronoun meaning "you" in the plural form.  
• "Dat" is a demonstrative pronoun meaning "that."  
• The sentence structure is: [Verb] [Subject] [Object/Complement]?  
• Example Sentences:  
  - "Vinden zij het mooi?" (Do they find it beautiful?)  
  - "Vinden jullie het eten lekker?" (Do you find the food tasty?)  
  - "Vindt hij de film interessant?" (Does he find the movie interesting?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Vinden jullie de muziek te luid?" (Do you find the music too loud?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it is common to express opinions using "vinden" to discuss likes, preferences, or perceptions with friends or in informal settings.

sentences.nl: Is dit voor jullie de eerste keer in Amsterdam? — “Voor mij wel”, zegt Pedro.
sentences.en: Is this your first time in Amsterdam? — “For me, yes,” says Pedro.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Is this for you (plural) the first time in Amsterdam? — "For me yes," says Pedro.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence starts with "Is dit," a question structure where the verb "is" precedes the subject "dit" (this), typical for yes/no questions in Dutch.  
• "Voor jullie" uses the preposition "voor" (for) combined with "jullie" (you, plural), indicating for whom something is intended or relevant.  
• "De eerste keer" translates to "the first time," using the definite article "de" before "eerste keer" (first time).  
• "Voor mij wel" means "For me, yes," where "wel" is used for affirmation in contrast to a potential negation.

Extra phrases:  
- "Is dit jouw boek?" (Is this your book?)  
- "Voor hem is het belangrijk." (For him, it is important.)  
- "De eerste keer is altijd spannend." (The first time is always exciting.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Is dit de eerste keer dat jullie dit proberen? (Is this the first time you are trying this?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Amsterdam is a popular tourist destination, known for its canals, museums, and liberal culture. Asking someone if it's their first time in Amsterdam can be a common conversation starter among tourists and locals.

sentences.nl: “Voor mij is het ook de eerste keer”, zegt Natasha.
“Voor ons ook”, zeggen François en Alice.
Mijn vader heeft familie in Amsterdam.
sentences.en: My father has family in Amsterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Mijn vader heeft familie in Amsterdam.  
• My father has family in Amsterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Mijn vader" means "my father," where "mijn" is a possessive pronoun.  
• "Heeft" is the third person singular form of "hebben," meaning "to have."  
• "Familie" refers to family members in general, not just the immediate family.  
• "In" is a preposition used for locations.  

Examples:  
• Hij heeft een huis in Utrecht. (He has a house in Utrecht.)  
• Zij hebben vrienden in Parijs. (They have friends in Paris.)  
• Mijn moeder werkt in een ziekenhuis. (My mother works in a hospital.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Mijn zus studeert in Leiden. (My sister studies in Leiden.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Amsterdam is the capital city of the Netherlands and is known for its cultural heritage, including historic canals, museums, and vibrant arts scene. Living or having family in Amsterdam might imply access to diverse cultural experiences.

sentences.en: Let's start.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "Laten we beginnen." → "Let us start."

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Laten" is the imperative form of the verb "laten," used to form suggestions or invitations. It is similar to saying "let's" in English.  
• "We" is the subject pronoun meaning "we" or "us."  
• "Beginnen" is the infinitive form of the verb "to start" or "to begin." In this construction, it follows "laten" to indicate the action.  
• Similar structure:  
  - "Laten we gaan." (Let's go.)  
  - "Laten we eten." (Let's eat.)  
  - "Laten we het proberen." (Let's try it.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Laten we dansen." (Let's dance.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, using "laten we" is a common and polite way to propose an activity or make a suggestion in a group setting.

sentences.en: We are going for a walk.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We go a round walk.  

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "We gaan" is an example of the present tense, which can indicate a future action or a habitual action.  
• "Een rondje lopen" literally translates to "walk a round," a common Dutch phrase meaning to take a short walk, often for leisure.  
• Word order: "We gaan een rondje lopen" follows the SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) structure.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ik ga een broodje eten." (I am going to eat a sandwich.)  
  - "We gaan naar het park." (We are going to the park.)  
  - "Zij gaat een boek lezen." (She is going to read a book.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "We gaan een film kijken." (We are going to watch a movie.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, taking a "rondje lopen" can be a social or relaxing activity, often done in parks or nature areas. It's a common leisure activity, reflecting the Dutch appreciation for outdoor activities and socializing.

sentences.nl: En ik vertel iets over Amsterdam.
sentences.en: And I tell something about Amsterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And I tell something about Amsterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "En" is a conjunction meaning "and," used to connect clauses or phrases.  
• "Ik vertel" is the present tense of "vertellen," meaning "I tell" or "I am telling." In Dutch, the subject "ik" (I) precedes the verb.  
• "Iets" means "something." It is an indefinite pronoun used for non-specific things.  
• "Over" is a preposition meaning "about" in this context. It indicates the subject or topic being discussed.  
• "Amsterdam" is a proper noun and requires no article.

Examples:  
• "En zij leest een boek." (And she reads a book.)  
• "Ik vertel een verhaal over mijn vakantie." (I tell a story about my vacation.)  
• "Hij praat iets over geschiedenis." (He talks about history.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En ik schrijf iets over Rotterdam." (And I write something about Rotterdam.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Amsterdam is not only the capital of the Netherlands but also a major cultural and financial center. It's often discussed in terms of its canals, museums, and vibrant history.

sentences.nl: Dit is het centrum van Amsterdam.
sentences.en: This is the center of Amsterdam.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is the center of Amsterdam.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is" means "This is," where "dit" is a demonstrative pronoun for "this" in neuter singular.  
• "het centrum" means "the center," where "het" is the definite article used for neuter nouns.  
• "van" is a preposition meaning "of" and indicates possession or relation.  
• "Amsterdam" is a proper noun and does not change form.

• Extra phrases/sentences:  
  - "Dit is het huis van mijn broer." (This is the house of my brother.)  
  - "Het centrum van de stad is druk." (The center of the city is busy.)  
  - "Dit is het boek van de leraar." (This is the book of the teacher.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dit is het begin van de dag." (This is the beginning of the day.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Amsterdam's city center is known for its historic canals, narrow houses, and vibrant culture. It's a popular tourist destination with a mix of historical and modern attractions.

sentences.nl: Kijk uit! Hier zitten veel duiven.
sentences.en: Watch out! There are a lot of pigeons here.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Look out! Here sit many pigeons.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Kijk uit" is an imperative form meaning "look out" or "watch out". It's commonly used to warn someone of danger.  
• "Hier zitten" translates to "here sit," indicating location. The verb "zitten" is used in Dutch to describe the position of something.  
• "Veel" means "many" and is used to indicate quantity.  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Pas op! Er ligt glas op de grond." (Watch out! There is glass on the ground.)  
  - "Hier staan veel bomen." (Here stand many trees.)  
  - "Er zijn veel mensen op het plein." (There are many people in the square.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Let op! Er zijn hier veel fietsers." (Be careful! There are many cyclists here.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In many Dutch cities, pigeons are common in public squares and can sometimes be considered a nuisance because they gather in large numbers and can make areas dirty.

sentences.en: This square is called 'the Dam'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This square is-called 'the Dam'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit plein" means "this square." "Dit" is the neuter form of "this," and "plein" is a neuter noun.  
• "Heet" is the third person singular form of the verb "heten," which means "to be called."  
• Proper nouns, like 'de Dam,' often follow the verb in sentences of this structure.

Examples:  
- Deze straat heet 'Kalverstraat'. (This street is called 'Kalverstraat'.)  
- Dat gebouw heet 'Rijksmuseum'. (That building is called 'Rijksmuseum'.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Deze rivier heet 'de Maas'. (This river is called 'the Maas'.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Dam is a famous square in the heart of Amsterdam, known for its historical significance and as a central meeting point.

sentences.nl: Dit is het ‘Monument op de Dam’.
sentences.en: This is the 'Monument on the Dam'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is the 'Monument on the Dam'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence starts with "Dit is," which is a common way to introduce or point out something in Dutch.  
• "Het" is the definite article "the" for neuter nouns.  
• "Op de Dam" translates to "on the Dam," where "op" is a preposition meaning "on" and "de Dam" refers to a specific location in Amsterdam.  
• Example sentences:  
  - Dit is mijn huis. (This is my house.)  
  - Het boek ligt op de tafel. (The book is on the table.)  
  - Dit zijn mijn sleutels. (These are my keys.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dit is het ‘Rijksmuseum’. (This is the 'Rijksmuseum'.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "Monument op de Dam" refers to the National Monument on Dam Square in Amsterdam, which is a war memorial commemorating World War II victims. It's a significant historical and cultural site in the Netherlands.

sentences.nl: Dit is het ‘Paleis op de Dam’.
sentences.en: This is the 'Royal Palace on the Dam'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is the 'Palace on the Dam'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is" is a simple present tense construction meaning "This is."  
• "het" is the definite article "the" used for neuter nouns.  
• "Paleis op de Dam" means "Palace on the Dam," with "op" meaning "on" and "de Dam" referring to a specific location in Amsterdam.  
• Example: "Dit is mijn huis." (This is my house.)  
• Example: "Dit is de beste plek." (This is the best place.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dit is het museum aan de gracht. (This is the museum on the canal.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The "Paleis op de Dam" is a famous historical building located in the heart of Amsterdam. Originally built as a city hall, it later became the royal palace where official functions occur. It's an iconic symbol of Dutch history and architecture.

sentences.en: No, that's a joke!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• No, that is a joke!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "Nee" is a direct way to say "No" in Dutch.  
• "Dat is" translates to "that is," where "dat" is a demonstrative pronoun.  
• "Een grapje" means "a joke," with "een" being the indefinite article and "grapje" being a diminutive of "grap" (joke).

Extra phrases:  
- "Dat is een auto." (That is a car.)  
- "Nee, ik wil niet." (No, I don't want to.)  
- "Hij maakt een grapje." (He is making a joke.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Ja, dat is een verrassing! (Yes, that is a surprise!)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Humor in the Netherlands is often dry and sarcastic, and jokes are a common part of daily conversation.

sentences.nl: Dit is een paleis van de koning.
sentences.en: This is a palace of the king.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is a palace of the king.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is" means "This is," where "dit" is the pronoun for "this" in Dutch.  
• "Een paleis" translates to "a palace" with "een" being the indefinite article "a."  
• "Van de koning" means "of the king," where "van" translates to "of" and "de koning" refers to "the king." This structure is used to show possession.  
• Example: "Dit is een boek van de leraar." (This is a book of the teacher.)  
• Example: "Dat is een auto van mijn vader." (That is a car of my father.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dat is een foto van de stad." (That is a photo of the city.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Netherlands has several palaces associated with the royal family, the most notable being the Royal Palace in Amsterdam, which is used for official functions.

sentences.en: The king has many palaces.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The king has many palaces.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De koning" is the subject and means "the king."  
• "Heeft" is the third-person singular present tense of "hebben," which means "to have."  
• "Veel" is an adjective meaning "many" or "a lot."  
• "Paleizen" is the plural form of "paleis," meaning "palaces."  
• Word order follows the standard Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) structure.

Extra Sentences:  
• "De kat heeft veel speelgoed." (The cat has many toys.)  
• "De lerares heeft veel boeken." (The teacher has many books.)  
• "Hij heeft veel tijd." (He has a lot of time.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De koningin heeft een groot paleis." (The queen has a big palace.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In the Netherlands, the royal family holds a ceremonial role, and the king's palaces are often used for state functions and official events.

sentences.en: This is a well-known park.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is a known park.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is" is a common Dutch structure meaning "This is."  
• "Een bekend park" translates to "a known park," where "bekend" is an adjective meaning "known" or "famous." In Dutch, adjectives usually precede the noun they describe.  
• Dutch uses the indefinite article "een" similar to "a" or "an" in English.  

Examples:  
– Dit is een groot huis. (This is a large house.)  
– Dit is een nieuw boek. (This is a new book.)  
– Dit is een oud gebouw. (This is an old building.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Dit is een beroemd museum. (This is a famous museum.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Parks in the Netherlands are often well-maintained and serve as popular places for leisure and community events. They are integral to Dutch city planning, offering green spaces in urban areas.

sentences.en: The 'Vondelpark'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The 'Vondelpark'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Het" is the definite article "the" in Dutch, used for neuter nouns.  
• "Vondelpark" is a proper noun and does not change form. In Dutch, park names are often preceded by "het" if they are neuter nouns.  
• Examples:  
  - Het Rijksmuseum (The Rijksmuseum)  
  - Het Anne Frank Huis (The Anne Frank House)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Het ‘Rembrandtplein’. (The 'Rembrandt Square')  

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Vondelpark is a famous public park in Amsterdam, often visited for leisure and cultural events. It's comparable to Central Park in New York City.

sentences.nl: In de zomer, kun je hier lekker uitrusten.
sentences.en: In the summer, you can relax here nicely.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• In the summer, can you here nicely rest.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "In de zomer" means "in the summer" and sets the time frame, using a prepositional phrase.  
• "Kun je" is an inversion of "je kunt," a common structure in Dutch questions and conditional sentences.  
• "Lekker uitrusten" combines "lekker" (nicely) with "uitrusten" (to rest), showing that "lekker" can be used to enhance the verb.

• Example 1: "In de winter, kun je hier schaatsen." (In the winter, you can skate here.)  
• Example 2: "Na het werk, kun je thuis lekker ontspannen." (After work, you can relax nicely at home.)  
• Example 3: "Op zaterdagochtend, kun je rustig ontbijten." (On Saturday morning, you can have breakfast peacefully.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• In de herfst, kun je hier mooie wandelingen maken. (In the fall, you can take beautiful walks here.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No related culture notes.

sentences.nl: “Wij willen nog niet uitrusten!” zeggen de studenten.
sentences.en: "We don't want to rest yet!" say the students.

sentences.nl: Wij willen nog heel veel zien.
sentences.en: We want to see a lot more.
The students walk further.
"How old is Amsterdam?" asks Natasha.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• "How old is Amsterdam?" asks Natasha.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence is a direct question followed by a reporting clause. "Hoe oud" (how old) is a question phrase.  
• The verb "is" (is) follows the subject "Amsterdam" in typical Dutch question word order.  
• "vraagt" (asks) is the third-person singular form of the verb "vragen" (to ask).  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hoe laat is het?" (What time is it?)  
  - "Wat zegt de leraar?" (What does the teacher say?)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Hoe ver is het strand?" vraagt Jan. (How far is the beach? asks Jan.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Amsterdam is a city with a rich history, known for its canals, architecture, and museums. Many visitors are curious about its age due to its historical significance.

sentences.en: Very old!

sentences.nl: Maar, de 17e eeuw was een belangrijke periode.
sentences.en: But the 17th century was an important period.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But, the 17th century was an important period.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions
